learning_objective: 🎯 Decode the secret language of DNA! Learn how traits are passed from parents to children and discover the rules of genetics set by Gregor Mendel.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Heredity is the passing of traits (like eye color or height) from parents to offspring. Information is carried in DNA segments called Genes, located on Chromosomes.
Gregor Mendel, the 'Father of Genetics', used pea plants to study inheritance. He chose them because they have easily observable, contrasting traits (like tall/short, green/yellow seeds).

A Dominant trait (e.g., Tall - T) expresses itself even if only one copy of the gene is present. A Recessive trait (e.g., Short - t) only expresses itself if both copies of the gene are recessive (tt).

A cross focusing on a single trait. When Mendel crossed pure Tall (TT) and pure Short (tt) plants, the first generation (F1) were all Tall (Tt). In the second generation (F2), the ratio of Tall to Short was 3:1.

Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes. The 23rd pair determines sex. Females have XX, and males have XY. If a sperm carrying an X fertilizes the egg (X), it's a girl (XX). If a Y sperm fertilizes it, it's a boy (XY). The father determines the sex of the child.

fun_activity.title: 👅 The Tongue Rolling Test
fun_activity.instructions: Try to roll the sides of your tongue into a U-shape. Can you do it? Ask your parents if they can. Tongue rolling is a genetic trait! If you can do it, you have the dominant gene.

exam_tips: 📌 Always practice drawing the Punnett square for a Monohybrid cross (3:1 phenotypic ratio).
📌 Differentiate between Genotype (genetic makeup, e.g., Tt) and Phenotype (physical appearance, e.g., Tall).
📌 Be ready to explain why the father, not the mother, determines the sex of the baby in humans.
quick_recap: ⭐ Variations during reproduction form the basis of inheritance and evolution.
⭐ Traits acquired during a person's lifetime (like a scar or playing guitar) are NOT passed to the next generation.
⭐ Mendel's laws proved that traits are inherited independently of each other.
